criterion: Happy-path-only (Meszaros) — the never-forced push is unproven
finding: No test ever lets `git push` meet a remote tip it does not contain, so adding `--force` to the push in `_push` passes all 48 tests. I ran that mutant on a copy, and the test named `test_open_never_forces_over_a_remote_fix_branch_it_does_not_contain` passed too, because the read-first check stops the step before any push runs.
why: docs/afk/small-lane/plan/0007-ship-script.md Acceptance: "Land fetches, checks the push is a fast-forward and pushes with upstream set by plain git, never forced, refusing a protected target; a non-fast-forward refusal is reported to the caller"; SDD §9b row "Feature-branch push": "remote refuses a non-fast-forward".
fix: Add a test in which the remote tip moves between the read-first `ls-remote` and the push. For example, wrap `ship._git` so the first `ls-remote` answers empty, then push a stranger commit from a second clone. Assert that the remote tip is still the stranger commit, nothing is listed, and the status is not-fast-forward or blocked. The `--force` mutant must then fail.
evidence: skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:325 `done = _git(cwd, "push", "--set-upstream", remote, f"HEAD:{ref}", check=False)`; skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:345 `return retry_with_read_back(write, read_back, read_first=True, sleep=tools.sleep)`; scripts/tests/test_ship.py:338-339 `assert result["status"] == "blocked" and "does not contain" in result["reason"]` / `assert remote_tip(repo, BRANCH) == stranger and forge.writes() == []`. Probe on a copy: mutant `"push", "--force", "--set-upstream", remote` -> `force SURVIVED | 48 passed`.

Either add an Acceptance or Produces line to docs/afk/small-lane/plan/0008-standalone-fix.md (SHIPPING.md: run `ship.py ready` as a tracked background job), or record a wiring IOU anchored to 0008 that names `ship.py ready`. finding: Land checks only `protected-lookup`, never whether Base is a feature branch. When the forge says the repository's base branch is unprotected, as on a repository with no branch protection, `ship.py land` on a diagnosis whose Base is `main` fast-forward-pushes the fix straight onto `main`. That push bypasses any change. A developer can run the script by hand, so reaching this does not depend on /afk:fix routing.
why: SDD.md §5 AuthZ: "| Merge | nobody | everybody | structural: no forge adapter has a merge verb |"; SAFETY.md "Change landing": "Use one branch and one Draft change by default ... A fix landed on a feature branch is covered by that feature's one Draft change." (that covers a feature branch only); SDD.md §3 /afk:fix row: "for a diagnosis started from a feature branch: the pushed commit and that branch, no ticket, no change"; scripts/protected-lookup.py:228-232 returns a definite forge answer `protected: false` for an unprotected branch, with no fallback to main/master.
fix: In step_land, refuse when the target equals the repository's base branch (`git.base-branch` through afk-config, or the remote's default branch) as well as when it is protected. Add a test: an unprotected `main` Base is refused with nothing pushed.
evidence:
skills/afk/fix/scripts/ship.py:551-554: "def step_land(d: Diagnosis, tools: Tools, cwd: Path) -> dict:
    head = _on_branch(cwd, d)
    target = _branch_name(cwd, d.base)

criterion: lifecycle: lookup constrained to the intended state
finding: _change_by_branch is documented as returning None when there is no change, but it passes any closed or merged change the by-branch lookup returns to _writable, which raises blocked. On proof's feature-branch path, a Base branch whose only change is closed or merged therefore ends `blocked` instead of `no-change` with the text for the run report. On open's path the advice to 'remove its Outside writes entry by hand' names an entry that does not exist, because that path runs only when no change is listed. Inferred, not checked against gh source: `gh pr view <branch>` falls back to the newest closed or merged PR when none is open. forge_ledger's twin of this lookup already handles that answer.
why: SDD.md:119 "feature-branch fix: one comment on that branch's open change, else the run report"; the repo's own lookup with the same contract treats a closed or merged answer as no open change: forge_ledger.py:1861-1867 "The open change for `tracked`, or None when the forge confirms there is none." ... `if str(view.get("state") or "").lower() in NOT_WRITABLE: return None`

criterion: error paths: an error read as an empty result
finding: Proof treats `missing: true` from change-view as proof that the Base branch has no open change and exits 0 with `no-change`. The GitLab adapter sets `missing` on any stderr that contains `404` or `not found`. A project lookup failure therefore turns proof into a silent `no-change`, and on the feature-branch path proof is the first forge call (land is plain git), so the broken forge goes unnoticed. Failing input: `gitlab.remote` names a project the token cannot read, and glab answers with a 404 Project Not Found error (exact glab wording unverified).
why: adapters/forge/gitlab/CONTRACT.md:67 "`change-view` answers `missing: true` in its error only when `glab` says no merge request exists for the reference."; SDD.md:119 "one comment on that branch's open change, else the run report" (only when no open change exists, not when the lookup failed).
fix: Narrow the GitLab adapter's missing pattern to the merge-request phrases (`no open merge requests?|merge request .*not found`) and drop the bare `404|not found`, so that CONTRACT.md:67 holds. Alternatively, before returning no-change, have proof confirm that the forge answers for a known reference (for example auth-status), and block otherwise.
evidence: ship.py:366-367 `if isinstance(answer, dict) and answer.get("error") and answer.get("missing"):` / `return None`; ship.py:477-479 `if found is None:` / `return {"status": "no-change", "reason": f"{target} has no open change; put the text "`; adapters/forge/gitlab/forge.sh:287 `printf '%s' "$reason" | grep -qiE 'no open merge requests?|merge request .*not found|404|not found' && missing=true`; ship.py:73 `EXIT = {"done": 0, "skipped": 0, "draft": 0, "no-change": 0, ...`

criterion: partial-failure handling: re-run after a write that took effect
finding: The push read-back finds an earlier push only when the remote tip equals HEAD. Suppose an earlier land pushed HEAD but its listing was lost, and someone has since pushed on top. The re-run then reports `not-fast-forward ... nothing pushed` and sends the caller to rebase and run every tier, although HEAD is already on the target. A probe on a real bare remote confirmed this. Open's push has the same gap: it blocks with 'did not take effect' when the remote fix branch already contains HEAD.
why: ship.py:34-35 "not-fast-forward (the Base branch moved: rebase once, run every tier, then land again)"; outside_writes.py:50-52 "`read_back()` answers ... an adapter answer object when it found the write". Here the write took effect, but the read-back reports a failure.
fix: In read_back, before the `moved` branch, return `{"ok": True, "commit": head}` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor head tip` succeeds (HEAD is already contained in the remote tip).
evidence: ship.py:335-343 `if tip == head:` / `return {"ok": True, "commit": head}` ... `if _git(cwd, "merge-base", "--is-ancestor", tip, head, check=False).returncode == 0:` / `return None` / `return {"error": True, "moved": True, "tip": tip,`; ship.py:564-566 `if isinstance(pushed.answer, dict) and pushed.answer.get("moved"):` / `return {"status": "not-fast-forward", ... "reason": f"{pushed.answer['reason']}: not a fast-forward, nothing pushed"}`. Probe (scratch lc0007/probe.py, case A: HEAD pushed to feat/export, then another clone pushed one commit on top): `A {"step": "land", "status": "not-fast-forward", ... "reason": "origin/feat/export is at 92df5c130faa, which ae39b5371172 does not contain: not a fast-forward, nothing pushed"}`
